title: isScriptLike still false-negatives on obvious recitals for statement-type cards (compare/challenge/evidence): those types skip the '?' check entirely, so a missed recital cue is their ONLY remaining defense, and the fixed cue list is easy to miss -- case-sensitive substring match ('Tell the student' does not match lowercase mid-sentence 'tell the student') and no coverage for plain imperative 'Say the X is Y.' forms (only the literal 'Say:' / 'Say to' substrings are cued)
evidence: direct read-only execution of the WORKTREE's own packages/schemas/src/guards.ts via tsx (no edit made): isScriptLike("Say the international office deadline is March 1.", "evidence") -> false (expected true); isScriptLike("You must tell the student their application is rejected.", "evidence") -> false (expected true); isScriptLike("tell the student to apply now.", "evidence") -> false (expected true). Control case isScriptLike("Tell them LSE is the right choice.") -> true (correct, confirms the harness), and the reviewer's 3 original strings + the definitive-tag-question case all still classify correctly per the manifest's claims.
fix: case-insensitive cue matching (or normalize to lowercase before .includes()), and widen RECITAL_CUES to catch plain imperative recital forms ('Say the ...', 'tell the ...' anywhere in the string, not just as an exact prefix/substring) -- or, for compare/challenge/evidence types, keep a stricter secondary signal since they have no '?' fallback to catch what the cue list misses
